1.why: All six screens are static card layouts with no animations or pop-ups, though the dark "Logs" debug panel with a long hex token adds some clutter.

2.why: Bold step headings, labeled fields, a single teal primary button per screen, and a highlighted safety-reminder box make the key elements stand out.

3.why: Each screen has one clear task, but the recovery code the user needs is buried as a 64-character hex string in a dark monospace "Logs" panel labeled "Test reset token".

4.why: Rules and steps are displayed inline so little must be memorized, but five password rules and a four-step flow with a 64-character code still impose notable load.

5.why: No password-manager option, autofill hint, or "remember me" checkbox appears on any of the six screens.

6.why: No saved items are shown, but the repeated layout and persistent Logs entries keep the delivered codes visible and recognizable across steps.

7.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences (e.g., "The code expires quickly and can only be used once"), with only minor jargon like "MFA code".

8.why: No error message appears in any of the six observed steps, so there is no error text describing a problem or its fix.

9.why: A placeholder ("Email address or phone contact") and an explicit password-rules box hint at input format, but no concrete example values are provided for any step.

10.why: Only one authentication path exists and each step presents a single clearly labeled action, though alternative choices such as face login are not offered at all.

11.why: Every screen contains exactly one input field and one primary button, so the user never faces more than one decision at a time.

12.why: Each action advances to a clearly titled next step and the final screen explicitly states "Password reset complete," though intermediate success is implied by navigation rather than stated.

13.why: Every step opens with a short instruction line and includes tip-style boxes (password rules, safety reminders), though there is no dedicated help link.

14.why: "Start over" and "Begin another recovery session" links allow restarting, though no mid-step error recovery is demonstrated.

15.why: All six screens share the identical header, card, button styling, reminder box, Logs panel, and footer, giving a fully consistent design.
